source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Strong clinical skill, teaching ability, and willingness to mentor, rather than simply picking whoever is available as the colleague is currently suggesting","B":"Having fairly little meaningful impact on new employee success, contrary to why preceptor selection is actually approached carefully in the first place","C":"Selecting whichever nurse is available without much regard for interest, similar to what the colleague is currently suggesting for this preceptor assignment","D":"Considering just years of experience, with fairly little other factor, which understates the other important qualities actually considered in this kind of selection"}}
source_row.rationale: Effective preceptor selection generally considers not only strong clinical competency, but also effective communication and teaching skills, and a genuine willingness and interest in mentoring others — since strong clinical skills alone do not guarantee someone will be an effective teacher or supportive mentor for a new employee's successful transition and development.
source_row.source_detail: Key Qualities for Effective Preceptor Selection
source_row.source_name: Nursing Professional Development Foundations — Preceptor Selection Criteria
source_row.stem: A nurse manager is selecting an experienced staff nurse to serve as a preceptor for a new employee, and a colleague suggests just picking whoever happens to be free that week regardless of their interest in teaching.
